'''Ehab Abouheif''' (born 28 July 1971 in [[Montreal]], Canada), is a Canadian [[biologist]] and Professor in the Centre of Organismal and Evolutionary Biology at [[Zhejiang University]], China. He is a specialist in integrating ecology, evolutionary, and developmental biology of [[Ant|ant societies]] in order to understand the origins and evolution of complex [[biological system]]s.<ref name = Guggenheim>{{cite web|url=https://reporter.mcgill.ca/guggenheim-for-ant-evolutionist/|title=Guggenheim for ant evolutionist : McGill Reporter|website=Publications.mcgill.ca|date=7 April 2017|access-date=14 August 2018}}</ref> He served as founding President of the Pan-American Society for Evolutionary Developmental Biology,<ref name = EvoDevoPanAm>{{cite web|url=http://www.evodevopanam.org/about-us.html|title=About us|website=evodevopanam.org|access-date=29 July 2023}}</ref> as well as co-founder for the McGill Centre for Islam and Science.<ref name = MCIS>{{cite web|url=http://www.islam-and-science.org/ |title=McGill Centre for Islam and Science is coming soon |publisher=Islam-and-science.org|access-date=2022-05-02}}</ref>

==Education==
Abouheif completed his bachelor's degree (1993) and a Masters (1995) with Honors at [[Concordia University]] in Canada. In 2002, he received a PhD in biology from [[Duke University]]. In 2002, he began postdoctoral studies at the [[Howard Hughes Medical Institute]] at the [[University of Chicago]], completing it in 2003 at the [[University of California, Berkeley]]. In 2004 Abouheif was appointed Assistant Professorship at [[McGill University]] as [[Canada Research Chair]] (tier II) in [[Evolutionary developmental biology|Evolutionary Developmental Biology]]. Previously, he was James McGill Professor in the Department of Biology at McGill University.<ref name = Guggenheim/><ref>{{cite web|url=https://kli.ac.at/content/people/all_people/view/25.|title=Discover The KLI|website=Kli.ac.at|access-date=15 December 2017}}</ref><ref name=CV>{{cite web|url=http://biology.mcgill.ca/faculty/abouheif/Abouheif_CV_01Feb2017.pdf|title=CURRICULUMVITAE : EHAB ABOUHEIF|website=Biology.mcgill.ca|access-date=15 December 2017|archive-date=14 December 2017|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20171214014305/http://biology.mcgill.ca/faculty/abouheif/Abouheif_CV_01Feb2017.pdf|url-status=dead}}</ref> He is currently a Professor at [[Zhejiang University]].<ref>{{cite web |title=Members - Centre of Organismal and Evolutionary Biology, Zhejiang University |url=https://evolution.zju.edu.cn/en/members.html |access-date=16 August 2026}}</ref>

==Research==
His research on "supersoldier ants" made a breakthrough in 2012 and revealed the importance of ancestral genetic potentials, which are stored and lay dormant in the genome for millions of years in almost all organisms. Abouheif discovered that with the right environmental triggers these potentials can be released and converted to ancestral-like phenotypic variation. Once released, ancestral genetic potentials can then be harnessed by selection to promote adaptation and evolution. Currently, Abouheif is trying to uncover the molecular mechanisms for the storage and release of ancestral genetic potentials in biological systems, and is working to harness these potentials to advance animal/plant breeding, medicine, and biodiversity conservation.<ref name = Guggenheim/>

==Honors and service==
Abouheif has been awarded national and international awards: the [[Sloan Fellowship]] (USA; 2006), the Steacie Fellowship (Canada; 2014), the [[Guggenheim Fellowship]] (USA; 2017), and was elected as a Member of the [[Royal Society of Canada]] (2016), the College of New Artists, Scholars and Scientists,.<ref name = Guggenheim/><ref name=CV/> He served as founding President of the Pan-American Society for Evolutionary Developmental Biology,<ref name = EvoDevoPanAm/> as well as co-founder for the McGill Centre for Islam and Science.<ref name="Guggenheim" /><ref name = MCIS/>
